analysis:
The supplied units are documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md (head excerpts at lines 4927-5333 and 5334-5437, plus the small patch at ~2966 adding the oneBuild gate) and docs/developer/test.md (new Cluster Pair Coordinated Update test section, lines 1043-1085). No executable code, keys, wire formats or authorization logic change in the supplied evidence, so no concrete security regression is identified.

Relevant claims for later passes (not verified here, since the underlying Swift sources are not supplied): (1) Qwen media reservations keep encoded bytes only in the request owner and rank 0, with `ClusterWorkerReservation.withDeadline` re-timing only the deadline. This touches A-001 and TB-007. (2) Prefix reuse is disabled for the cluster media ingress (`ClusterWorkerPrefixCache.disabled`), which is consistent with T-041 and does not widen the cross-tenant cache channel. (3) The per-request native-context charge and the refusal path (503 for that request alone) bear on availability. (4) A pair-serving grant is required before a coordinator forms a pair, which is consistent with the TB-011 and T-052 posture. (5) The coordinated pair update (cluster-always-on.md, ClusterPairUpdateCycle) is described only in the tests doc: staging, admission closure, drain, install and rollback on both Macs. It touches T-043 (rollback authority is the same replaceable binary) and T-013. The start check runs the temporary install's `darkbloom --version`, which is a script in tests only.

Integration questions: the actual pair-update implementation, its partner-state trust (whether a partner's claim of staging or automatic-updates-off is authenticated over the cluster link), and whether the oneBuild check cannot be abused to stall updates. These live in source files outside this batch. T-043's threat entry may deserve a note for the new coordinated-update path if that code lands. I raise no finding, since the evidence is only prose.
